author: TIM SEAMAN
title: MidAmerican confirms data center discussion in Salix - NewsBreak
text:
By TIM SEAMAN Maren Ewertz ,
19 hours ago
SALIX , Iowa ( KCAU ) — Woodbury County is a step closer to being home to a data center.
MidAmerican Energy Company has disclosed that it is involved with a proposed development site near the city of Salix, being evaluated for possible development as a data center site.
For the second time in less than a month, Salix City Council members were hard-pressed to provide any information concerning the recently annexed property, leaving those in the room upset and, in some cases, angry.
Close to 100 people filled the Salix City Hall Chambers again with questions and concerns.
Discussion on a possible data center was reserved for the public comment portion of the meeting, leaving council members unable to directly answer any questions.
Story continues below
Mayor Kevin Nelson did confirm that a rezoning request is needed before a project like this can begin has not come before the council. Though that didn’t go far in lessening concerns voiced by residents.
Steve Peterson, a concerned Salix resident, said, “How will having a data center preserve and protect our agricultural and ecological resources around the Salix area?”
“If this area is developed into a data center, is that the legacy that you want to leave for your future family members or future Salix residents?” asked Janet Yanek, another concerned Salix resident.
“I’ll have a conversation with any of you,” said Mitch Ler, a concerned Salix resident. “I respect each and every person in this room, because that’s what we have to do.”
Information made available to those in attendance Wednesday night lists hundreds of construction jobs, new tax revenue, increased traffic for local businesses, and infrastructure improvements as benefits to the community if a data center were to be built on the annexed property.
Now, MidAmerica wouldn’t operate the data center. Rather, they would sell electricity to a future customer who would develop the site.
PREVIOUS: ‘Go ask those landowners’: Salix residents grill city council on potential annexation A MidAmerican representative at Wednesday night’s meeting calls this the “First inning” of the process, adding that once a customer joins the project, more information will be available.
“Unfortunately, I can’t define a timeline right now. It could be a couple of months, it could be several months if it ever happens. We hope to select a customer as soon as we can so that that customer can come in here and answer a lot of those questions,” said MidAmerican Energy representative Adam Jablonski.
“There’s a long process, and that’s after the zoning change happens, which hasn’t even been presented yet because there is no end user,” said City of Salix Mayor Kelvin Nelson.
Nelson again emphasized that a rezoning request has not been presented to the city and that until that time, the council will take no action.
KCAU 9 will continue to follow the developments of the potential data center in Salix, both on air and right here on our website.
